Worcester Family Court

Quick Reference Information

  • Address: 225 Main St, Worcester, MA 01608, United States
  • Phone: (508) 831-2200
  • Hours: Monday-Friday, 8:30 AM – 4:30 PM (Closed weekends and holidays)
  • Email: wpfc@jud.state.ma.us
  • Website: http://www.mass.gov/
  • Google Maps: 7682+X3 Worcester, Massachusetts, USA

Introduction to Worcester Family Court

Worcester Family Court, officially known as the Worcester Probate and Family Court, serves Worcester County, Massachusetts, covering over 60 cities and towns. The court handles all family-related legal matters with the goal of resolving disputes fairly while protecting the rights and interests of all parties involved.

Types of Cases Handled

Divorce Proceedings

Massachusetts follows “no-fault” divorce laws, meaning you only need to state that your marriage has irretrievably broken down to file for divorce. The court handles:

  • Property division
  • Alimony determinations
  • Divorce mediation
  • Contested and uncontested divorces

Child Custody and Visitation

The court makes custody decisions based primarily on the child’s best interests, considering:

  • Parent-child relationships
  • Child’s preferences (if age-appropriate)
  • Each parent’s ability to provide for the child’s needs
  • Stability and continuity factors
  • Parenting plans and schedules

Child Support

Child support determinations consider:

  • Both parents’ income
  • Number of children
  • Parenting time arrangements
  • Children’s healthcare costs
  • Childcare expenses
  • Special needs considerations

Spousal Support (Alimony)

The court determines alimony based on factors including:

  • Marriage duration
  • Each spouse’s income and earning potential
  • Standard of living during marriage
  • Each spouse’s financial needs
  • Contributing factors to the end of marriage

Domestic Violence Protection

For victims of domestic violence, the court provides:

  • Restraining order applications and hearings
  • Emergency protection orders
  • Referrals to support services and counseling
  • Safety planning assistance

Visiting the Courthouse

Parking Options

  • Pearl-Elm Municipal Garage: Located diagonally across from the courthouse (paid parking)
  • Federal Plaza Parking Lot: One block from the courthouse (paid parking)
  • Metered Street Parking: Available on surrounding streets (2-hour limit, quarters or ParkMobile app required)

Public Transportation

  • MBTA Commuter Rail: Worcester Union Station (Framingham/Worcester line) is 0.5 miles from courthouse
  • WRTA Bus Service: Multiple routes stop near Main Street and Franklin Street

Courthouse Preparation

  • Plan to arrive 30 minutes before your scheduled appearance
  • Bring all relevant documents (court notices, legal papers, identification)
  • Dress appropriately (business casual, no shorts, tank tops, or hats)
  • Silence electronic devices before entering courtrooms
  • Be prepared for security screening upon entry

Key Court Services

Probate Division

  • Will validation and contests
  • Estate administration
  • Guardianship appointments
  • Adoption proceedings
  • Legal name changes
  • Trust administration

Family Division

  • Divorce filings and proceedings
  • Child custody determinations
  • Child and spousal support orders
  • Paternity establishment
  • Modification of existing orders

Virtual Registry Services

Worcester Family Court offers digital services through its Virtual Registry:

  • eFiling for existing cases
  • Court date reminder text notifications
  • Online docket and calendar searches
  • Virtual assistance from court staff
  • Form downloads and submissions

Fees and Payment Options

  • Filing fees vary by case type
  • Payment methods: cash, check, money order, credit/debit card
  • Online payments through ePay system
  • Fee waivers available for qualifying low-income individuals (Affidavit of Indigency required)

Accessibility and Accommodations

Contact Language Access Coordinator Megan Brown:

  • Fax: (508) 752-6138
  • Email: megan.brown@jud.state.ma.us
  • Interpreter services available in over 200 languages

Domestic Violence Resources

If you’re experiencing domestic violence, the court provides several resources:

  • Emergency restraining orders (available 24/7 through local police)
  • Safety planning assistance
  • Connections to local shelters and support services
  • Referrals to counseling and support groups
  • Coordination with victim advocates

Probation Department Services

The court’s Probation Department handles:

  • Juvenile cases (delinquency, Children Requiring Assistance)
  • Domestic abuse monitoring
  • Mental health referrals
  • Case investigations and recommendations
  • Compliance monitoring

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: How do I file for divorce in Worcester Family Court? A: You can file divorce papers in person at the courthouse or through the eFiling system. Massachusetts requires completion of forms including the Complaint for Divorce and financial statements.

Q: Can I represent myself in Family Court? A: Yes, many people represent themselves (“pro se”). The court offers resources for self-represented litigants, including form assistance and procedural guidance.

Q: How long does the divorce process typically take? A: Uncontested divorces may be completed in 3-6 months. Contested divorces involving property, custody, or support disputes can take 1-2 years depending on complexity.

Q: How do I modify an existing child support or custody order? A: File a Complaint for Modification showing a substantial change in circumstances since the original order was issued.

Q: Are cell phones allowed in the courthouse? A: Yes, electronic devices are permitted after security screening, but must be silenced in courtrooms.

Tips for Court Success

  1. Be punctual: Arrive early for all hearings and appointments
  2. Organize your documents: Bring multiple copies of all relevant paperwork
  3. Follow courtroom etiquette: Address the judge as “Your Honor” and speak only when addressed
  4. Prepare concise statements: Be clear and direct when presenting your case
  5. Consider mediation: Many family disputes can be resolved more amicably through court-connected mediation services

Conclusion

The Worcester Probate and Family Court provides essential legal services for families throughout Worcester County. Understanding the court’s procedures and preparing properly for your case can help ensure a smoother legal process. For specific legal advice, consult with an attorney or the court’s self-help resources.
